info.title: blt API
info.description:
blt collects backup jobs and inventory from backup products (Commvault,
Rubrik) into one database. **This API is the only thing that reads or
writes that database.** Collectors never touch Postgres: they ask the API
where they left off, post what they collected, and report how the run
went. Reports and other readers use the same API.

## Signing in

Every endpoint except `/healthz` needs the API key in an `X-API-Key`
header. In these docs: **Authorize** (top right), paste the key, and the
*Try it out* buttons send it.

```
curl -H "X-API-Key: $BLT_API_KEY" \
    https://api.blt.lab.ethos.home/v1/sources/commvault/cv-toaster/last-run
```

## Conventions

- **Sources are named in the path**:
  `/v1/sources/{source type}/{source name}/...` - a CommCell is
  `/v1/sources/commvault/cv-toaster`, an RSC account
  `/v1/sources/rubrik/work`. The name is blt's own (its Prefect
  block's), not the product's. Each source type has its own endpoints
  below that, in its product's own terms.
- **Times** are ISO 8601 with a time zone (`2026-10-29T14:00:00Z`). A
  time in a request body without one is refused.
- **Lists** page with `limit` and `offset`.
- **Errors** come back as `{"detail": "..."}`: 401 for a missing or wrong
  key, 404 for an unknown source, run or job, 422 for a body or
  parameter that does not validate.
- **Writes are upserts**, keyed by the source's own ids. Posting the same
  batch twice changes nothing; a batch collected *before* what is
  already stored is ignored, so a slow run cannot roll a job back.

## Versions

Everything except `/healthz` is under `/v1`. Changes that don't break a
client (a new endpoint, field or optional parameter) are made in `/v1`
as it stands. A change that would break one goes into a `/v2` beside
it, and `/v1` stays until every collector has moved over.

The paths from before versioning (`/commcells/{name}/...`,
`/rubrik/{name}/...`) still work, for collectors on an older release.
They answer with a `Deprecation: true` header, are not listed here, and
will be removed.

## One collection run

1. `GET .../last-run` - the watermark: where the last successful run
   started. None means never collected.
2. `POST .../runs` - open a run; keep its `id`.
3. `POST .../jobs` - the jobs collected, in batches, each with the run id.
4. `POST .../runs/{run_id}/finish` - succeeded or failed. Only a
   succeeded run moves the watermark.

Commvault runs also check on jobs still active (`GET .../jobs?active=true`)
and reconcile ones the CommCell no longer knows (`PATCH .../jobs/{job_id}`).
Rubrik runs need neither: RSC reports every change, so one pass covers it.

resume_from.title: Resume From
resume_from.description: Where the next backfill chunk should end: the oldest point already covered. Null: nothing collected yet.

backfilled_to.title: Backfilled To
backfilled_to.description: How far back a backfill has reached. Null: no backfill has run.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: The start of the CommCell's history has been reached.

BackfillState.title: BackfillState
BackfillState.description:
How far back a CommCell's history has been collected.

`resume_from` is where the next backfill chunk should end: the oldest
point already covered, whether by a backfill or by ordinary runs.
None means nothing has been collected yet, so there is nothing to
backfill behind.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: The start of the CommCell's history has been reached.

BackfillUpdate.title: BackfillUpdate
BackfillUpdate.description: How far back a backfill has now collected.

client.title: Client
client.description: The client the instance is on.

job_id.title: Job Id
job_id.description: Its most recent full backup job. Null or 0: never backed up.

discovered.title: Discovered
discovered.description: Databases the source knows on the instance.

backed_up.title: Backed Up
backed_up.description: Of those, how many this job backed up (matched by name).

reported_backed_up.title: Reported Backed Up
reported_backed_up.description: Commvault's own count of databases the job backed up.

reported_skipped.title: Reported Skipped
reported_skipped.description: Commvault's own count of databases the job skipped.

missed.title: Missed
missed.description: Databases known on the instance that this job did not back up.

unconfirmed.title: Unconfirmed
unconfirmed.description: Databases that cannot be checked by name (system databases).

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Anything else worth knowing about this row, in words.

observed_at.title: Observed At
observed_at.description: When the inventory run that produced this row finished.

InstanceReportRow.title: InstanceReportRow
InstanceReportRow.description:
One database instance and its most recent full backup: how many
databases the source knows on it, how many that backup took, and
which ones it missed.

`backed_up` counts the known databases whose last full is this job,
by name. `reported_backed_up` / `reported_skipped` are the backup
product's own totals for the job, kept alongside as a cross-check
rather than trusted on their own. System databases cannot be checked
by name (the source gives them no per-database job), so they are
counted in `discovered` and reported separately in `unconfirmed`.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: The run this batch belongs to: the `id` from `POST .../runs`.

collected_at.title: Collected At
collected_at.description: When this was read from the source. Nothing older than what is already stored overwrites it.

been collected for this CommCell, i.e. do a full run.

ValidationReport.title: ValidationReport
ValidationReport.description:
Protection as judged from one source's own account of itself.

Today the only witness to what exists is the backup product, so this
can find what that product knows about and has not protected. It
cannot find what the product has never seen; `inventory_at` and
`sources` are here so a reader can tell how much the answer rests on.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: ok: backed up within the allowed age. stale: backed up, but longer ago. unprotected: known to the source, with no backup. empty: an instance with no databases known under it. unverified: in backup content, but the source gives no per-object backup time (SQL Server system databases). gone: the latest inventory no longer lists it.
